article.articleHeadline: أول تجربة على البشر للقاح سلالة نادرة من إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: First human trial of a vaccine for a rare Ebola strain
article.articleSummary: First human trial of a vaccine for a rare Ebola strain begins in Oxford, with 50 healthy adults aged 18-55; it evaluates safety and immune response of the Chadox1 PDBPV vaccine candidate. Recruitment is underway; vaccinations are expected in coming weeks pending regulatory approval. The candidate uses the same viral-vector platform as the Oxford/AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. Serum Institute of India produced and stored about 620,000 doses within two weeks, providing 4,000 doses for the initial phase. In May, the World Health Organization prioritized Chadox1 PDBPV alongside a single-dose candidate RVSV Bondidpiojo for clinical evaluation as part of outbreak response. The Alliance for Pandemic Preparedness Innovations pledged up to $8.6 million to support development. Preparatory studies are planned in Uganda, pending regulatory approvals. If the early phase succeeds, partners will advance to later-stage trials for emergency use authorization or full approval, aiming for rapid, affordable supply to affected countries.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスの稀な株に対するワクチンの初の人体試験
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は稀なエボラ株に対するワクチン候補の臨床試験開始に関するもので、新規感染アウトブレイクではなく、研究開発イベントである。対象国内での実際のエボラ感染症発生を報告していない。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはワクチン候補（ChAdOx1 PDBPV）の臨床試験プロトコルの説明であり、実際の感染症アウトブレイク事象ではない。オックスフォードでの試験開始、ウガンダでの準備研究計画、インドでのワクチン生産が記載されているが、これらは研究開発段階の活動であり、シグナル検知の対象とはならない。発生地域にUganda、India、UKが含まれるが、実際のエボラ感染症発生は報告されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Invité Afrique Midi - Ebola en RDC: "Le combat à Kisangani est de limiter la mobilité et détecter tous les cas suspects", selon le ministre de la Santé
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Guest on Afrique Midi - Ebola in the DRC: "The fight in Kisangani is to limit mobility and detect all suspected cases," according to the Minister of Health.
article.articleSummary: Four confirmed Ebola cases in Kisangani, the densely populated capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Tshopo Province. The infections are linked to Nia-Nia, a health zone in Ituri, located about 350 kilometers away. The confirmation of Ebola in Kisangani prompts intensified public health actions, with authorities aiming to limit movement and to detect all suspected cases. Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba spoke with Patient Ligodi, detailing the response priorities. The report highlights rapid isolation, case finding, and comprehensive contact tracing to curb transmission as the outbreak extends from Ituri to Kisangani. No mortality figures or laboratory methods are provided beyond the four confirmed cases.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ・ミディ出演 - DRCのエボラ出血熱: 「キサンガニでの戦いは移動制限と疑い例の全数検出」と保健大臣が語る
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がイトゥリ州から350km離れた人口密集都市キサンガニに拡大し、4例確認。ヒト-ヒト感染のリスクが高く、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: イトゥリ州ニア・ニア保健区から350km離れた人口密集都市キサンガニへのエボラ拡大が確認された。移動制限や接触者追跡などの対応が進行中。死亡者数や検査方法の詳細は記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Patient wird in Frankfurter Uniklinik behandelt
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola patient is being treated at Frankfurt University Hospital
article.articleSummary: An American Ebola patient is being treated at Frankfurt University Hospital on a dedicated isolation unit. The patient contracted the Bundibugyo variant of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and arrived in Frankfurt around 3:00 a.m. on Monday; his condition is stable. U.S. authorities asked the German government for help, citing Frankfurt's special isolation facility, one of seven nationwide. In May, a similarly infected American was treated at Charité Berlin. Health insurers cover the substantial treatment costs. No public risk: the patient is fully isolated; wastewater is processed in tanks, waste is securely disposed of, and building exhaust is filtered through two systems. Staff report emotional and physical strain but are trained for such events; inter-state transport and handover drills are routine. There is no approved antidote or vaccine; care is supportive, addressing fever, pain, and diarrhea; a 2014 case required ventilation and dialysis, but recovered.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ患者、フランクフルト大学病院で治療中
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でブンディブギョ株エボラウイルスに感染した米国人患者がドイツへ医療搬送されており、国際的な感染拡大・搬送事例として、DRCでの流行状況を確認するためフルRRAに進めるべき。
triage.notes: 本記事はドイツでの隔離治療体制に焦点を当てているが、感染源はDRCであり、ブンディブギョ株エボラの発生状況・規模について続報確認が必要。5月にもベルリンで同様の搬送事例があったとの記載から、複数の国際医療搬送が発生している可能性があり、DRC国内の流行実態の把握が重要。

article.articleHeadline: 全球醫療焦點！剛果民主共和國爆發伊波拉疫情　美籍患者送德治療 - 民視新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Global medical spotlight! Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo; American patient sent to Germany for treatment.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has expanded to Haut-Uele and Tshopo provinces. As of July 13, 2026, 1,926 laboratory-confirmed cases and 702 deaths have been reported. A U.S. citizen working for a humanitarian organization contracted Bundibugyo strain Ebola virus, becoming the first imported/exported case and was transported to Frankfurt University Hospital in Germany for isolation and treatment. The U.S. CDC is coordinating with the patient’s organization and DRC authorities to prevent further spread. Separately, Oxford University announced the first human clinical trial of the BD-Ebov vaccine targeting Bundibugyo/Ebola, enrolling 50 healthy adults aged 18–55 to assess safety and immune response, aiming to bolster responses to outbreaks in Congo and neighboring Uganda.

triage.headline_ja: 全球医療焦点！コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱が流行、米国人患者はドイツで治療
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で確定例1,926人・死亡702人に達する大規模エボラ流行が複数州に拡大し、米国籍患者がドイツへ輸送された初の国際輸出例が発生。IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し、国際的関心も高い。
triage.notes: ドイツ・米国・ウガンダは輸出/近隣国として言及されているが、発生国はDRCのみであり対象国リストにはDRCのみ含まれる。

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يوسع دائرة انتشاره في الكونغو الديمقراطية.. 1926 إصابة مؤكدة وتحذيرات من تفاقم الأزمة الصحية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola widens its spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo — 1,926 confirmed cases and warnings of worsening health crisis.
article.articleSummary: As of July 13, 2026, Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo sums to 1,926 laboratory-confirmed cases and 702 deaths, with four new cases in the Out-Wili region and two deaths among Chobo cases; one death in Out-Wili is reported. The outbreak, the country’s seventeenth, began May 15 and initially centered in Ituri, later spreading to North Kivu and South Kivu, before extending to Out-Wili and Chobo. Investigations suggest many new infections in the two regions trace back to Nyania in Ituri, but authorities treat Out-Wili and Chobo as part of the same outbreak. The World Health Organization cautions the true scale may be larger, given possible missing links to earlier cases. Transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids; health teams are intensifying surveillance, contact tracing, and response readiness, with international support urged to curb the spread.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国で拡大 — 確定感染者1,926人、健康危機悪化への警告
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱が拡大し、確定患者1,926人・死者702人と重大な公衆衛生上の影響があり、複数地域への拡大とヒト-ヒト感染リスクがあるため、IHR基準を複数満たしフルRRAへの移行が適切。
triage.notes: 発生地域にGhana, Angolaが含まれるが記事本文ではDRCのみが主題であり、他国での発生は確認されないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Response Faces Strikes as Trials Begin
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak in eastern Congo intensifies with Ituri frontline workers staging a 24-hour strike over unpaid wages and poor working conditions. Clinics report capacity strain as payroll disputes intersect with the response. The outbreak, declared in May, has expanded to multiple provinces, complicating containment and patient care. Trials begin enrolling Ebola treatments, including remdesivir and MBP134, as international partners (WHO, INRB, Oxford) push for rapid enrollment, though finance flows lag and community mistrust hampers outreach and data collection. The government says payrolls are being validated and payments will reach the appropriate workers, even as investigation and verification continue. Independent reports note a lack of vaccines or established treatments for Bundibugyo Ebola, underscoring the urgency of effective clinical trials amid ongoing transmission. The situation remains fluid with ongoing transmission across multiple provinces.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ対応、治験開始の中でストライキに直面
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのブンディブギョ型エボラ出血熱の流行が複数州に拡大し、ヒト-ヒト感染が継続、ワクチン・治療薬未確立で国際機関が治験を進めている状況であり、公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクが高い。
triage.notes: ウガンダも発生地域として挙げられているが、記事本文はコンゴ東部（イトゥリ州等）での流行拡大が主題であり、ウガンダでの発生は明記されていないため除外。ワクチン・確立治療法が存在しない点、資金不足・医療従事者ストライキによる対応能力低下が懸念材料。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: Oxford University starts 1st human trial of new Ebola vaccine
article.articleSummary: On 13 July 2026, Oxford University launched the first-ever human trial of a vaccine against Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BD-Ebov). The Phase I study will assess safety and immunogenicity in a cohort of 50 healthy adults aged 18–55, amid ongoing Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. The BD-Ebov vaccine candidate, ChAdOx1 BDBV, was developed by Oxford's Vaccine Group and Pandemic Sciences Institute and uses the same chimpanzee adenovirus vector platform as the Oxford/AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. The Serum Institute of India manufactured and stockpiled about 620,000 doses within two weeks and supplied 4,000 investigational doses for this early-stage trial.

triage.headline_ja: オックスフォード大学、新型エボラワクチンの初のヒト臨床試験を開始
triage.triage_reason: 記事の主題はワクチン臨床試験の開始であり、DRC・ウガンダでの進行中のブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス（BDBV）アウトブレイクは背景情報として言及されているのみで、アウトブレイク自体の詳細（規模・死亡者数等）が不明のため続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 疾病名タグ『COVID-19』はワクチンプラットフォームの共通性（ChAdOx1ベクター）を指すものであり誤タグ。実際のイベントはブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス（BDBV）ワクチンの第I相臨床試験開始に関するもの。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRC・ウガンダでのアウトブレイクの現状（規模・死亡者数等）に関する続報が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Alemanha recebe segundo norte-americano infetado com Ébola vindo do Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Germany receives the second American infected with Ebola coming from Congo.
article.articleSummary: Germany received a second American citizen infected with the Ebola virus from the Democratic Republic of Congo, now hospitalized at the University Hospital of Frankfurt in stable condition. The transfer occurred about two months into the outbreak declared in May in eastern DRC; the patient is a humanitarian worker, with identity not disclosed, per US CDC. German authorities say there is no population risk and that transmission risk is very low, and the transport was incident-free. The current outbreak has 1,926 confirmed cases and 702 deaths in DRC, with 753 in isolation and 318 recovered. The outbreak began in Ituri and has reached Uganda, with 20 cases and two deaths. The WHO notes the Bundibugyo strain, with a 30–50% fatality rate, and currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment. WHO has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern; the risk is high in sub-Saharan Africa, global risk is low. Transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include hemorrhagic fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and internal bleeding. The outbreak is not controlled until 42 days pass with no new cases.

triage.headline_ja: ドイツ、コンゴ由来エボラ出血熱に感染した2人目の米国人を受け入れ
triage.triage_reason: DRCでWHOがPHEICを宣言したエボラ出血熱の大規模流行が継続中で、ウガンダへの拡大や国際的な患者搬送も発生しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: アウトブレイクはDRC東部（イトゥリ州）で発生し、ウガンダに拡大（対象国リスト外）。ドイツ・米国は患者搬送先であり発生国ではないため除外。WHOはPHEICを宣言済みで、Bundibugyo株による致死率30-50%の重症流行。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: سباق علمي لمواجهة إيبولا.. جامعة أكسفورد تبدأ اختبار لقاح جديد وسط تفشي الفيروس في الكونغو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Scientific race to combat Ebola: University of Oxford begins testing a new vaccine amid an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
article.articleSummary: Oxford University in the United Kingdom plans to start testing an experimental Ebola vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain amid an ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Initial safety studies will enroll 50 healthy volunteers aged 18–55 in the UK to assess safety and immunogenicity, with the trial designed to yield early indications of protection within weeks. The effort accompanies a stockpile of about 620,000 doses of the ChAdOx1 BD-BV vaccine prepared for potential large-scale use, and roughly 4,000 experimental doses reserved for Oxford-led trials. Researchers are coordinating with partners in Uganda to plan possible clinical studies in Africa, a region heavily affected by Ebola outbreaks. Volunteers in the UK will be followed for one year; preliminary signals of efficacy are expected soon. The vaccine uses the same ChAdOx1/AstraZeneca platform as COVID-19, enabling rapid vaccine development when outbreaks emerge.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ対策の科学的競争:オックスフォード大学がコンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ流行の中、新ワクチンの試験を開始
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)のアウトブレイクが進行中であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と異常事象という2つのIHR基準に該当するため、フルリスク評価への移行が適切。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はDRCで進行中のエボラ流行を背景としたオックスフォード大学によるワクチン臨床試験（UKで実施）。UKは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。ウガンダは将来的な臨床試験のパートナーとして言及されているのみで、現時点でウガンダでの発生は確認されていないため除外。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: Reino Unido avança com ensaios clínicos da vacina contra o Ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: United Kingdom advances with clinical trials of the Ebola vaccine.
article.articleSummary: UK regulator authorized a first-in-human trial of a new Ebola vaccine targeting Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with Oxford’s BD-Ebov study launching in the United Kingdom. Phase I will enroll 50 healthy adults aged 18–55 in Oxford to assess safety and immunogenicity, with first doses expected within weeks. This vaccine is the first of four to enter clinical testing amid an outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda, which has 1,792 laboratory-confirmed cases and 625 deaths. The effort follows a WHO Public Health Emergency; trials are planned with Ugandan partners. Its platform uses a chimpanzee adenovirus vector—used in the COVID-19 vaccine—to express an Ebola protein and elicit immunity. Serum Institute of India is manufacturing and storing about 620,000 doses.

triage.headline_ja: 英国、エボラワクチンの臨床試験を開始
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国・ウガンダで進行中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（確定例1,792件、死亡625件、WHO PHEIC）に関連し、深刻な公衆衛生影響と国際的拡大が確認されるため。
triage.notes: 記事の主眼は英国オックスフォードでのエボラワクチン第I相試験開始（BD-Ebov）だが、背景として既存のコンゴ民主共和国・ウガンダにおけるエボラアウトブレイク（WHO PHEIC）に言及。ウガンダ・英国・インドは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。インドはワクチン製造拠点であり発生国ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Prefeito Renato Junior testa positivo para Covid-19 e entra em isolamento em Manaus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mayor Renato Junior tests positive for COVID-19 and enters isolation in Manaus
article.articleSummary: Manaus Mayor Renato Junior tested positive for COVID-19 and will isolate for three days. He developed fever, sore throat, and dry cough over the weekend. The city administration said his oxygen saturation remains normal and his clinical condition is good, with remote work planned during recovery. He is up to date with COVID-19 vaccination and following medical guidance. He will continue monitoring municipal affairs remotely, without in-person engagements. The mayor's health updates will be provided through official channels if necessary. The city urged individuals with respiratory symptoms to seek medical care and to maintain precautions to reduce transmission of COVID-19 and other respiratory diseases.

triage.headline_ja: マナウス市長ヘナート・ジュニオール氏、新型コロナウイルス陽性で隔離入り
triage.triage_reason: 市長個人の軽症COVID-19感染事例であり、公衆衛生上の異常性や重大性、拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 個人の健康状態に関する報道であり、公衆衛生上のシグナルとしての意義は低い。COVID-19は既知の疾病であり、市長は軽症で経過良好、ワクチン接種済み。

article.articleHeadline: Alemanha recebe segundo cidadão norte-americano infectado com Ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Germany receives the second American citizen infected with Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Germany welcomed a second American citizen infected with Ebola from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), at the request of the United States, according to the German Ministry of Health. The transfer comes about two months after the first American patient was transported to Germany amid an Ebola outbreak declared in mid-May in eastern DRC. The ministry said the patient, whose identity was not disclosed, was admitted on Sunday to Frankfurt University Hospital. U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) indicated the patient is a humanitarian aid worker in the DRC, but offered no further details. The Frankfurt hospital said the patient is showing Ebola symptoms but is in a stable condition.

triage.headline_ja: ドイツがエボラに感染した2人目のアメリカ人を受け入れ
triage.triage_reason: DRC由来のエボラ出血熱感染者が国際搬送される事案が続いており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し、国際的拡大の懸念がある。
triage.notes: 患者はDRCで発生したエボラアウトブレイクに関連する人道支援活動者であり、ドイツへの国際医療搬送が2例目となる。ドイツ・米国は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : la riposte à court d'argent, un plan financé à 35 %
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: the response lacking funds, a plan funded at 35%
article.articleSummary: DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak, as of July 11, records 1,926 confirmed cases and 702 deaths. The response plan, a joint government-WHO effort worth $510 million for June–November, stands funded at only about 35% by mid-June, leaving numerous health zones in Ituri and North Kivu without adequate treatment centers. In Bunia and Rwampara, frontline workers protested unpaid incentives, delaying operations and signaling broader funding gaps; authorities promised direct-payment professional cards to streamline disbursements. The Ituri civil-society confederation called for an independent financial audit and provincial oversight. The funding shortfall—around $20 million immediately—hampers all response pillars from laboratory work to logistics. No vaccine or specific therapy exists for the Bundibugyo strain; Ervebo covers Zaïre only. The PARTNERS trial is testing two experimental treatments since early July; routine measures—case detection, isolation, and contact tracing—remain the backbone, though capacity in Nord-Kivu is stretched and national contact-tracing sits at ~78.3%.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱:資金不足の対応、計画の資金充足率は35%
triage.triage_reason: DRCの第17次エボラ流行は確定例1,926人、死亡702人に達し、対応計画の資金は35%しか確保されておらず、治療体制の維持が困難な状況にあるため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断した。
triage.notes: 発生地域にRwandaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC（Ituri, North Kivu）のみでの感染拡大が述べられており、Rwandaでの発症は確認されていないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : le personnel de santé en première ligne, et en danger
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Healthcare workers on the front line and in danger.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reaches 1,926 lab-confirmed cases and 702 deaths as of July 11, 2026, marking the 17th DRC outbreak. Healthcare workers are heavily affected: 112 infections and 35 deaths (31.2% case fatality) due to nosocomial transmission amid PPE shortages, inadequate chlorine supply, and limited infection prevention training; in Musienene and Beni, North Kivu, adherence to infection prevention measures averages only 25%. In early July, response workers protested over pay and conditions, halting operations in Bunia and Rwampara and slowing care at the epicenter. The Ituri health system is strained; UNICEF warns Bunia’s sole pediatric daycare at Centre Medical Evangélique is saturated with infants infected or orphaned. Facility births in Bunia fell from about 130 to 30 per month, with rising maternal mortality. Do not suspend routine vaccines or polio/cholera efforts. Bundibugyo strain has no licensed vaccine or specific treatment; Ervebo covers Zaïre strain only, so protection relies on prevention, PPE, and steady workforce funding.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：最前線で危険にさらされる医療従事者
triage.triage_reason: DRCで進行中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（第17次）が1,926例・702死亡に達し、医療従事者への院内感染や対応の破綻など深刻化しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 発生地域にRwanda（Kigali Province）が含まれるが、記事本文はDRC（Ituri州、Bunia、North Kivu）での状況に限定されているため、Rwandaはverified_locationsから除外した。Bundibugyo株は既存ワクチン（Ervebo）の対象外であり、医療従事者の感染率・死亡率が高く、対応体制の崩壊（賃金未払いによる抗議活動）が事態を悪化させている点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Angajații unui spital din Congo unde sunt tratați pacienți cu Ebola, în grevă
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The employees of a hospital in Congo where Ebola patients are treated are on strike.
article.articleSummary: In Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, staff at General Hospital Rwampara—the Ebola treatment site—went on strike, including epidemiologists, case investigators, drivers, and a gravedigger, prompting hospital closure and road blockage. Workers report two months of unpaid salaries since May; authorities say payroll lists are being reconciled to ensure payments reach those involved, noting changes to names have sparked complaints. Separately, Congo declared a new Ebola outbreak on May 15, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccine exists. The country has recorded 1,926 confirmed cases and 702 deaths to date. Africa CDC described the outbreak as the fastest-spreading in Africa, highlighting rapid expansion amid ongoing control efforts.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ患者を治療しているコンゴの病院職員がストライキを実施
triage.triage_reason: DRCでBundibugyo株による新規エボラ流行が拡大中（1,926例・702死亡）で、Africa CDCが「アフリカ最速の拡大」と指摘。ワクチン未承認かつ治療拠点病院でストライキが発生し対応能力にも支障が出ており、IHR基準複数該当のためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株にはワクチンが存在せず、治療拠点病院での職員ストライキが対応の遅延要因となっている点は重要な注視ポイント。

article.articleHeadline: Nächster infizierter Ebola-Patient landet in Frankfurt - Sonderisolierstation übernimmt Behandlung
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Next Ebola-infected patient lands in Frankfurt - Special isolation ward takes over the treatment.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola-infected United States citizen is being treated at University Hospital Frankfurt since early Monday morning, 13 July 2026, in a special high-security isolation ward. The patient’s condition is stable; no age or sex details or full illness progression were disclosed, but symptoms align with Ebola and have not worsened since arrival. Treatment is supportive, focusing on fluids, nutrients, and symptom-directed care. Hospital leadership stressed no risk to the public, and the isolation unit operates with multiple safety levels to prevent pathogen escape, with fully protected medical staff. The patient arrived at Frankfurt Airport overnight and was transported to the hospital. This marks the second U.S. citizen flown to Germany for treatment within about two months. The U.S. CDC said the patient worked for a humanitarian organization in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and a test was positive for the Bundibugyo variant of Ebola currently circulating there.

triage.headline_ja: 次の感染したエボラ患者がフランクフルトに到着 - 特別隔離病棟が治療を担当
triage.triage_reason: DRCで流行中のエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)に感染した米国人が国際搬送によりドイツで治療を受けており、これは約2ヶ月で2例目の事例であり、国際的な感染拡大・搬送事例としてIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 患者はDRCで感染し国際的な人道支援活動中に感染、その後米国からドイツ・フランクフルトへ治療のため搬送された事例。ドイツ国内での二次感染リスクは病院側により否定されているが、DRCでのエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)流行が背景にあり、これが2ヶ月以内で2件目の同種搬送事例であることから、DRCでの流行状況の推移を含めたフルリスク評価が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : ce que l'on sait de Peter Stafford, le médecin humanitaire américain infecté et placé en isolement à Francfort
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: What we know about Peter Stafford, the American humanitarian doctor infected and placed in isolation in Frankfurt
article.articleSummary: As of July 13, 2026, an American citizen in his 60s infected with Ebola Bundibugyo from the Democratic Republic of Congo was admitted to the Frankfurt University Hospital isolation unit in Germany. His condition is stable and there is no public risk. The patient, a warehouse manager for Samaritan’s Purse, was evacuated after a Bundibugyo-positive CDC report. This is the second such case in recent weeks; in June another American treated at Berlin’s Charité after Congo exposure was discharged. In the DRC, the outbreak totals 1,926 lab-confirmed cases and 702 deaths, with spread to Haut-Uélé and Tshopo provinces. Oxford University began a first human trial of a Bundibugyo vaccine (BD-Ebov) with ChAdOx1 BDBV in 50 healthy adults; Serum Institute of India produced about 620,000 doses, supplying 4,000 for the study; CEPI will invest up to $8.6 million. No licensed vaccine or specific therapy exists; care remains supportive and experimental, focusing on early detection, isolation, and contact tracing.

article.articleHeadline: Oxford's new Ebola vaccine enters first human trial: Serum Institute making over 6,20,000 doses
article.articleSummary: ChAdOx1 BDBV, an Oxford University vaccine candidate against Bundibugyo ebolavirus, enters Phase 1 trials in Oxford, UK—the first vaccine against this strain to advance to humans. The trial follows the WHO's PHEIC declaration 57 days earlier and is backed by CEPI to evaluate safety and immunogenicity in 50 healthy adults aged 18–55; recruitment has begun and vaccinations are slated to start pending regulatory approval. Serum Institute of India produced and stockpiled about 620,000 doses in two weeks for potential emergency use and supplied 4,000 doses for the Phase 1 trial. The vaccine uses the ChAdOx chimpanzee adenovirus vector platform, the same as the Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. CEPI, Oxford and SII launched an $8.6 million partnership to fast-track development. Preparations for additional Uganda studies are under way with MRC/UVRI and LSHTM Uganda Research Unit. The ongoing Africa outbreak prompted a PHEIC declaration by the WHO.

article.articleHeadline: आंकड़ों में दिखी टीबी की असली चुनौती
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The real challenge of tuberculosis revealed by the data
article.articleSummary: As of July 13, 2026, Lucknow, India — Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge, with a 100-day intensive TB campaign showing that timely case finding and linkage to testing and treatment are the main hurdles. During the campaign, 280,000 residents were screened; 39,600 exhibited presumptive TB symptoms (persistent cough, fever, weight loss, loss of appetite, or coughing up blood). Of these, 9,370 new TB cases were laboratory-confirmed and linked to free treatment. Notably, 3,560 individuals without clear symptoms were also identified, enabling earlier intervention to curb transmission. The effort included 301 Ayushman Arogya camps and 1,924 Nikshay Mitr volunteers under the Prime Minister’s TB-Free India program, who collectively supported nutrition packs for 7,800 TB patients. Officials emphasize that active case finding and community participation are essential to breaking the transmission chain and achieving a TB-free India.

article.articleHeadline: Statement on the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo by Tom Fletcher, Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator, 9 July 2026
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues; declared 15 May. As of 9 July 2026, over 1,700 infections and 600 deaths in DRC. Ituri province remains the outbreak's center, with spread to other provinces amid conflict and population movement. Uganda has confirmed 20 cases. WHO and Africa CDC are supporting the epidemiological response under leadership. The Inter-Agency Standing Committee has activated a System-Wide Scale-Up; a Senior Ebola Coordinator has been deployed. The Emergency Response Fund has released up to $60 million to accelerate response in the DRC and preparedness in neighboring countries (Uganda, South Sudan, Burundi). Borders and supply routes must stay open; blanket travel bans hinder humanitarian operations. Donors should provide flexible funding promptly. Preparedness priorities include surveillance, laboratory testing, referral systems, infection prevention and control, and community engagement. Trust, local leadership, and protection from exploitation are essential to the response and to prevent further deaths.

triage.triage_reason: DRCで1,700人超の感染、600人超の死亡が確認され、ウガンダへの越境拡大も報告されている。国連機関による大規模スケールアップ対応が発動されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大なシグナル。

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يواصل تفشيه في الكونغو الديمقراطية ووفاة 702 جراءه
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola continues its outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 702 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola continues in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 1,926 confirmed cases and 702 deaths. Official data show spread to two additional northeastern provinces, Ou-Wili and Chobo, including four cases in Chobo (two deaths) and one death in Ou-Wili reported last Saturday. The outbreak, the 17th in DRC, began May 15 and remains centered in Ituri, with cases also reported in North Kivu and South Kivu. Kisangani, capital of Chobo, lies near Ou-Wili on the border with South Sudan and the Central African Republic. WHO says the true scale could be two to four times higher, as many new cases have no known link. Oxford University has begun a first human trial of a vaccine against Bundibugyo Ebola virus (ChAdOx1 BDVP), enrolling 50 healthy adults in Oxford; regulatory approvals awaited. Serum Institute produced about 620,000 doses; CEPI pledged up to $8.6 million to support development; Uganda trials planned.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、コンゴ民主共和国で流行継続、死者702人
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で第17次エボラ流行が拡大し、感染確認1,926例・死亡702例に達し新たな州にも拡大、南スーダン・中央アフリカ共和国との国境地帯に近接するなど国際的拡大リスクが高いため、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはUK（Oxford, England）やSudan, Angola, CAR, Ugandaが含まれるが、これらはワクチン試験地や国境隣接国として言及されているのみで、実際の感染発生はDRC国内（Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Ou-Wili, Chobo等）に限定されるためDRCのみをverified_locationsに含めた。

article.articleHeadline: Oxford launches first human trial of Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine
article.articleSummary: Oxford launches the first human trial of Bundibugyo ebolavirus vaccine BD-Ebov (ChAdOx1 BDBV) in 50 healthy adults in Oxford, UK, to assess safety and immune response; vaccinations are expected in coming weeks pending regulatory approval. Developed by Oxford's Vaccine Group and Pandemic Sciences Institute on the same viral-vector platform as the Oxford/AstraZeneca COVID shot, it is backed by Serum Institute of India, which supplied 4,000 investigational doses after manufacturing about 620,000. CEPI has pledged up to $8.6 million to support development, and WHO has prioritized ChAdOx1 BDBV alongside rVSV Bundibugyo for clinical evaluation amid the ongoing DRC–Uganda outbreak. Preparations are underway for additional Uganda studies via MRC/UVRI and LSHTM Uganda Research Unit. In the DRC, Haut-Uele and Tshopo are newly affected, bringing 1,926 confirmed cases and 702 deaths; the outbreak remains centered in Ituri with cases in North Kivu and South Kivu.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-Fall in Deutschland: US-Bürger nach Ankunft in Klinik behandelt
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola case in Germany: U.S. citizen treated after arriving at hospital
article.articleSummary: As of 13 July 2026, Germany is treating a second U.S. citizen with Ebola who arrived at Frankfurt Airport overnight and was transferred to University Hospital Frankfurt in Frankfurt, Hesse. The patient has been on a dedicated isolation ward since about 3:00 a.m.; condition is stable and disease has not progressed since arrival. Age, sex, and specific symptoms are not disclosed, but Ebola-typical symptoms are present. Treatment is supportive (fluids and nutrients) with monitoring of blood viral load; there is no vaccine or specific therapy for the Bundibugyo variant of Ebola virus. Officials say the public is not at risk; the isolation unit has multiple safety barriers. The patient works for a humanitarian organization in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where Bundibugyo-ebola has been detected; Congo reports 1,926 laboratory-confirmed cases, 702 deaths, 318 recoveries, and 753 currently treated. Earlier in May, a U.S. doctor was brought to Berlin Charité and discharged after about two weeks.

triage.headline_ja: ドイツでエボラ感染例：米国人がフランクフルト到着後に病院で治療
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で発生中のエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）が既に米国人患者を通じてドイツに輸入され、DRCでは1,926例・702人死亡という大規模な流行が継続しているため、フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: إضراب "عمال إيبولا" يفاقم أزمة تفشي الفيروس في الكونغو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola workers' strike worsens the Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Dozens of Ebola treatment-center workers at Rwampara General Hospital in Ituri, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, went on strike over unpaid salaries and allowances dating from May, prompting hospital closure after roadblocks. The protest involves epidemiologists, case investigators, drivers, and grave-diggers who report PPE shortages and perceived unfair treatment by authorities. Dr. Biensi Kanu, a member of the provincial outbreak surveillance committee, said pay requests have been pressing since the outbreak began, with delays causing economic hardship for families. Official data show 1,873 confirmed Ebola cases and 672 deaths this year; earlier figures cited 1,708 infections and 580 deaths. The strike compounds the outbreak as clinical trials test therapies for the Bundibugyo strain. WHO’s Dr. Anne Ansia says transmission continues due to population movement and security challenges, with several treatment centers at capacity; authorities warned of a 24-hour strike if dues remain unpaid.

triage.notes: エボラ治療センター職員の未払い給与によるストライキが対応能力に支障を与えており、WHO関係者も人口移動・治安問題による感染継続を指摘。ブンディブギョ株の臨床試験も進行中。

article.articleHeadline: Εκτός ελέγχου η επιδημία Έμπολα στο Κονγκό - Φόβοι ότι θα αποδειχθεί η χειρότερη όλων των εποχών
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Out of control Ebola epidemic in Congo – fears it will prove to be the worst of all time.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo reports Ebola Bundibugyo virus outbreak expanding to Haut-Uele and Tshopo, in addition to Ituri and North and South Kivu. Confirmed cases reach 1,926 with 702 deaths. The outbreak, declared May 15, is feared to be the worst on record. New cases in Tshopo (4 cases, 2 deaths) and Haut-Uele (1 death) raise concerns about cross-border spread to South Sudan and Central African Republic. Investigations suggest most cases in these two provinces are imported from Nyania, while Ituri remains an epicenter. Bundibugyo ebolavirus causes diarrhea, flu-like symptoms, followed by potentially fatal internal and external bleeding; case fatality estimated 30-50%. Silent transmission, with many patients staying home, may accelerate spread; WHO notes underestimation of true cases by 2-4x. In positive news, Oxford University began Phase I trials of an experimental vaccine; 50 volunteers in the UK, Uganda to follow; Serum Institute of India has produced 620,000 doses.

article.articleHeadline: Gefährliches Virus: Weiterer Ebola-Patient in Deutschland - Zustand stabil
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dangerous Virus: Another Ebola Patient in Germany - Stable Condition.
article.articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo virus case in Germany: A US citizen working for a humanitarian organization in the Democratic Republic of Congo tested positive and was treated at Berlin’s Charité after arriving May 20. Initially life-threatening during transport, he improved and was discharged after about two weeks; treatment is supportive (fluids and nutrients) with monitoring of blood viral load. There is no vaccine or specific therapy for Bundibugyo. The patient, his wife and four children—high-risk contacts—were quarantined in a separate station; officials say the public is not at risk. The trip used a specialized isolation setup. End of June, Bundibugyo virus was detected in Europe for the first time in France (doctor returning from East Congo), who was isolated and discharged in early July after negative tests. In DR Congo: 702 deaths, 1,926 lab-confirmed cases, 318 recovered, 753 currently in care. The outbreak’s rapid rise exceeds prior Ebola outbreaks; three Ebola patients have previously been treated in Germany: Uganda doctor (Frankfurt), Senegalese (Hamburg), and a Leipzig UN worker who died.

article.articleHeadline: Tshopo : les agents et cadres d'une commune appelés à sensibiliser leurs concitoyens contre Ebola - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tshopo: Municipal staff and officials called upon to raise awareness among their fellow citizens about Ebola - ACP.
article.articleSummary: In Kisangani’s Makiso commune, Tshopo Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, municipal staff and officials were urged by Mayor Simon Lowawa to mobilize residents against Ebola during the weekly parade, following a provincial decree on preventive measures. The message emphasized the urgency of Ebola and the need to break transmission chains; with no approved treatment or vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain, adherence to barrier measures is the only protection. Deputy Mayor Martin Luther Lituambela reinforced that neighborhood leaders should ban motorcycle taxi meetings and that tax collectors should intensify field sensitization. Sensitization at Kalindula block in Plateau medical neighborhood occurred Sunday; Plateau Boyoma will be the next step.

article.articleHeadline: Banda DM Colony Faces Dirty Water Supply for Five Days, Residents Demand Immediate Action | Banda News: डीएम कॉलोनी में 5 दिनों से गंदे पानी की सप्लाई, संक्रमण का खतरा बढ़ा
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Banda DM Colony Faces Five Days of Dirty Water Supply, Infection Risk Has Increased
article.articleSummary: Five days of contaminated, murky drinking water in Banda DM Colony, Banda city, in the Civil Lines area behind the GIC Hostel, have heightened concerns about waterborne diseases. Residents report foul-smelling, turbid water unfit for drinking or domestic use, forcing reliance on bottled water or external sources. They warn of rising risks of diarrhea, typhoid, and vomiting-with-diarrhea among children, the elderly, and others if supplies are not restored and water quality is not tested. Suspected pipeline leaks or sewer-water ingress are cited as possible causes, prompting calls for urgent pipe inspection and repairs plus laboratory testing of water quality. Residents urge immediate action from the district magistrate, the water board, and the municipality to restore safe, regular drinking water and avert a broader health crisis.

article.articleHeadline: East Singhbhum DC orders 24-hour malaria case reporting, treatment
article.articleSummary: East Singhbhum, including Jamshedpur, implemented 24-hour reporting of all confirmed malaria cases to the civil surgeon and initiation of treatment within 24 hours, as directed by deputy commissioner Rajiv Ranjan to contain spread. In a malaria prevention workshop, government and private facilities were urged to strengthen surveillance, reporting, and care; private hospitals attended. Civil surgeon Dr Sahir Pall will ensure immediate household surveillance around fever patients in malaria-hit blocks Potka, Dumaria, Musabani, Ghatshila, and Dhalbhumgarh and promote rapid diagnostic tests for prompt detection. Six malaria deaths have occurred (four cerebral malaria, two mixed infections) and are under review. Between June 29 and July 12, 104,459 people were screened; 96,478 via RDTs and 7,981 by microscopy, yielding 1,895 malaria cases (1,491 PF, 353 PV, 51 mixed), district positivity 1.96%. WHO official Dr Akhilesh urged vigilance in Jharkhand.

triage.headline_ja: 東シングブーム地区行政官、マラリア症例の24時間報告と治療を指示
triage.triage_reason: インド・ジャールカンド州で季節性マラリアの流行が継続し死亡例も出ているが、異常性や国際拡大リスクは低く、既存の行政対応（サーベイランス強化）の範囲内である。
triage.notes: マラリアは当該地域で季節性に発生する既知の疾患であり、蚊媒介感染症のため国境を越える伝播リスクは低い。死亡6例（脳性マラリア4例、混合感染2例）が報告され、地区陽性率1.96%。WHO職員が警戒を呼びかけているが、国際支援の具体的要請は記事内に確認できない。行政による24時間報告体制やRDT普及などの対応強化は通常の公衆衛生管理の範囲内と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : installation recommandée de points de contrôle sanitaire contre Ebola à Kambala - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: Recommended establishment of health checkpoints against Ebola in Kambala - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Two confirmed Ebola virus disease cases in Kambala health zone, Mahagi territory, Ituri province, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. As of 13 July 2026, one patient has recovered; the other is hospitalized at the Ebola Treatment Center (CTE) in Logo. No deaths reported; 94 contacts are actively followed. The hospitalized case is an imported infection from the Iga-Barrière trading center in Djugu territory, who had also stayed in Bule trading center before treatment. To prevent new introductions, health authorities recommended establishing sanitary checkpoints at Berunda, Plantation, Leku, Kambala-Centre and Katanga, with mandatory hand washing and temperature screening at entry points along main routes to epidemic epicenters. Additional measures sought: an ambulance, a dedicated isolation room, enhanced handwashing facilities in public institutions and major crossroads, and provision of potable water for health facilities. Investigation to identify all contacts continues.

triage.headline_ja: イツリ州：カンバラでのエボラ対策として保健検査所の設置が推奨される（ACP）

article.articleHeadline: T7News | Taubaté confirma a 10ª morte por dengue em 2026; cidade já soma mais de 4 mil casos prováveis
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: T7News | Taubaté confirms the 10th dengue-related death in 2026; the city already has over 4,000 probable cases.
article.articleSummary: Taubaté, Brazil dengue outbreak: 10th death in 2026; over 4,000 probable cases (4,096). The deceased is a 41-year-old woman from central Taubaté with no comorbidities. Death occurred May 19; cause officially confirmed July 7 after epidemiological investigation. In total 10 dengue deaths; six additional deaths are under investigation. Incidence 1,270.5 per 100,000; lethality 0.24% among probable cases and 11.90% among severe cases. Authorities urge Aedes aegypti control: cover water tanks, clean gutters, remove stagnant water, keep yards clean. Symptoms prompting care: high fever, body aches, retro-orbital pain, red rash, nausea, vomiting. Severe signs: intense abdominal pain, bleeding, drowsiness, or breathing difficulty require immediate medical attention. Control measures include breeding-site blockades, house-to-house visits, and case monitoring to curb the epidemic.

article.articleHeadline: 中國新冠確診 6月增7.9萬例
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China's COVID-19 cases rise by 79,000 in June.
article.articleSummary: China reports 79,000 new COVID-19 cases in June 2026, with 130 severe cases and 1 death. From June 1–30, 31 provinces plus the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps reported the June total; sentinel hospitals showed rising COVID-19 positivity among outpatient/ED influenza-like illness cases over Weeks 23–26 (2.9%, 4.1%, 5.3%, 6.4%). Genomic surveillance for June 1–30 yielded 3,741 valid local sequences, all identified as Omicron variant. In Week 27 (Jun 29–Jul 5), COVID-19 ranked second among respiratory pathogens in ILI samples at 9.6% positivity (flu 11.6%, enteroviruses 9.1%). Among hospitalized SARI respiratory samples, rhinovirus 7.1%, human metapneumovirus 5.4%, and influenza 4.5% were top pathogens. Due to past underreporting, public skepticism persists that the true situation may be worse. On July 12, COVID-19 topics trended on Weibo; discussions highlighted long-term effects, including immune disruption and chronic symptoms after infection.

The esthesiometer assesses peripheral nerve sensitivity to detect early neurological changes, track progression, and prevent disabilities. This acquisition, after more than ten years, supports the Municipal Hanseniasis Control Program and enhances the health system's capacity to respond through early detection and continuous care. Health Secretary Deisi Bocalon emphasized improved diagnostic quality and follow-up, while Adjunta de Atenção Primária Cinara Brito noted strengthened assessments and comprehensive care at the primary level—the main entry to SUS. No case counts are provided; the initiative aims to reduce sequelae as of 13 July 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Lutte contre la tuberculose en RDC : contextualisation du guide pratique d'engagement des médias - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Combating tuberculosis in the DRC: contextualization of the practical guide to media engagement - ACP
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa hosted a 9–11 July 2026 workshop contextualizing the Practical Guide for Media Engagement in the fight against drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) and an advocacy package under the RESPECT project (Resilient, People-centred, Community-Led Response to End DR-TB). Organized by Club des Amis Damien (CAD) with the National Tuberculosis Control Program (PNLT), the exercise aims to inform policy decisions, funding, and program acceptability while placing DR-TB in the media spotlight to boost public knowledge and demand for services. Dr Antoinette Olenga (PNLT) said the contextualized guide will help national programs, partners, civil society and communities implement effective DR-TB communication. Expected results include an operational DR-TB media plan and a durable partnership framework between PNLT, CAD and the media anchored in transparency and mutual respect. DR-TB is described as tuberculosis bacteria that no longer respond to standard antibiotics, typically due to poor treatment adherence.

article.articleHeadline: Bavarian Nordic Partner Submits Chikungunya Vaccine For Approval In Brazil
article.articleSummary: Eurofarma submitted Anvisa for approval of CHIKV VLP chikungunya vaccine for individuals aged 12 and older, with Bavarian Nordic continuing as manufacturer. The filing is supported by clinical data showing robust neutralizing antibody responses across age groups and a favorable safety profile. Brazil accounted for more than half of the worldwide 2025 chikungunya cases (over 500,000) and nearly 200 deaths, highlighting the target market. Under the January 2026 exclusive distribution agreement, Eurofarma handles regulatory work, commercialization, and distribution in Brazil; Bavarian Nordic remains the supplier, and Eurofarma has a right of first refusal for Latin America opportunities. CHIKV VLP is a single-dose, adjuvanted recombinant protein vaccine that is non-infectious; it is marketed as Vimkunya in the U.S., EC, UK, Switzerland, and Canada. Chikungunya causes fever, rash, and severe joint pain; 30–40% develop chronic symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Cette bactérie très ancienne devient vite résistante aux antibiotiques, alerte une étude
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: This very ancient bacterium rapidly becomes resistant to antibiotics, a study warns.
article.articleSummary: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi, typhoid agent, is acquiring resistance to most antibiotics, threatening oral treatment. Typhoid causes about 9 million cases and 110,000 deaths annually, transmitted by contaminated water and food; symptoms include prolonged fever, abdominal pain, and digestive disturbances; untreated fatality can reach 10–30%, while effective antibiotics reduce it to 1–4%. A 2022 genomic study of 3,489 isolates from Nepal, Bangladesh, Pakistan and India (2014–2019) and over 4,000 other genomes shows emergence of XDR strains resistant to first-line drugs, fluoroquinolones, and third-generation cephalosporins, with acrB mutations linked to azithromycin resistance rising in South Asia. First XDR detected in Pakistan in 2016; by 2019 dominant. Globally, 138 spreads and 59 intercontinental events trace to South Asia, with travel-linked cases in the UK, US, Canada and France since 2018. WHO recommends conjugate TCV; Pakistan added it in 2019 with Gavi support. Prevention emphasizes safe water and prompt post-travel fever evaluation.

triage.headline_ja: この非常に古い細菌は急速に抗生物質耐性を獲得している、とある研究が警告

triage.notes: 記事はフランスの一般向け科学報道で、2022年のゲノム研究（南アジア4か国の分離株解析）を基にした薬剤耐性チフス菌（XDR株）の拡大傾向を報告。パキスタン・ネパール・バングラデシュも主要発生国だが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。インドは分離株調査対象国として含めた。渡航関連症例は英国・米国・カナダ・フランスでも報告されているが、これらは対象国リスト外。

article.articleHeadline: La peste no es enfermedad erradicada y sigue matando
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The plague is not an eradicated disease and it continues to kill.
article.articleSummary: Plague (Yersinia pestis) persists in Madagascar, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and Uganda, with sporadic cases in western United States; globally up to 3,000 cases annually. In Madagascar, about 250–500 cases per year. The disease has three forms: bubonic (flea-borne with painful lymphadenopathy), septicemic, and pneumonic (lung infection, the only form with person-to-person transmission). Europe has been plague-free since 1945 (Corsica last reported cases); U.S. cases remain rare. A notable Oregon case followed a cat bite, was misdiagnosed as cat-scratch disease, and required intensive care; the patient survived. Early, nonspecific symptoms delay diagnosis; rapid lab confirmation and prompt antibiotics are essential. The Robert Koch Institute and Malagasy laboratories work to strengthen diagnostics and prevent imported/exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : un hélicoptère chargé de médicaments contre Ebola contraint de rebrousser chemin à Niania - LePotentiel
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: a helicopter carrying Ebola medicines forced to turn back on the way to Niania - LePotentiel
article.articleSummary: On July 13, 2026, in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of Congo, a helicopter carrying medicines for Ebola virus disease (EVD) response to the 17th outbreak was forced to turn back after residents in Niania, Mambasa territory, refused to land. The blocked delivery disrupted essential supplies for patient care and ongoing outbreak response. Despite sensitization campaigns, pockets of resistance persist where the disease is poorly understood, fueling rumors and mistrust of medical teams. Urgent, intensified community engagement is needed; traditional authorities, administrative leaders, religious figures, and civil-society groups should bolster outreach to gain acceptance of prevention and response measures. No official statements yet on the incident circumstances or on arrangements to ensure medicines reach Niania. Community involvement remains critical to interrupt transmission and strengthen the Ebola response.

article.articleHeadline: Second US citizen diagnosed with Ebola transferred to Germany for treatment: WHO
article.articleSummary: Second U.S. citizen diagnosed with Ebola, a humanitarian worker, diagnosed Friday in Congo with Bundibugyo virus and transported to Frankfurt University Hospital, Germany, for treatment; admitted early Monday and currently stable in a special isolation unit. The patient worked for Samaritan's Purse in Ituri province, Congo (Bunia and Nyankunde Ebola Treatment Centers; 40 beds each) in a logistics role for five years; Samaritan's Purse states he was not involved in direct patient care. WHO Director‑General Tedros emphasized protecting frontline responders amid the outbreak. Samaritan's Purse has operations in Congo; authorities, CDC, U.S. State Department, and Congolese government are coordinating, with contact tracing underway. The U.S. and White House have defended treating abroad due to proximity; the CDC's Title 42 order continues to route travelers from Congo/Uganda/South Sudan to screening; this case marks the second U.S. citizen diagnosed with Ebola in this outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: La peste no es enfermedad erradicada y sigue matando
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The plague has not been eradicated and continues to kill.
article.articleSummary: Plague (Yersinia pestis) persists globally with about 3,000 annual cases; Madagascar, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Uganda are heavily affected, with Madagascar reporting 250–500 cases annually and a major outbreak in 2017. Sporadic cases occur in western United States. An Oregon case illustrates diagnostic challenges: Paul Gaylord developed plague after cat exposure, was misdiagnosed as cat-scratch disease, deteriorated to coma, and survived after ICU care. The disease has three forms: bubonic (fleas transmit from infected rodents, causing painful lymphadenopathy), septicemic (bacteremia), and pneumonic (airborne droplets causing pneumonia; the only form with sustained human-to-human transmission). Europe has been plague-free since 1945 (Corsica last). Yersinia pestis traces back at least 5,500 years in skeletons. Diagnosis is challenging; rapid laboratory confirmation and early antibiotics are crucial. Research networks in Madagascar and at the Robert Koch Institute (RKI) aim to strengthen diagnostics and surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Why 1 American's Ebola case has the world worried
article.articleSummary: An American humanitarian worker with Bundibugyo Ebola, contracted in the Democratic Republic of Congo, was flown to Germany for care and admitted to Frankfurt University Hospital’s secure unit. The CDC confirmed infection during Congo’s ongoing outbreak, described as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, with 1,830 confirmed cases and at least 648 deaths as of July 13, 2026, and cross-border spread into Uganda. The Bundibugyo variant is rare and lacks an approved vaccine or treatment, complicating response amid funding gaps, attacks on health centers, and eastern Congo conflict. This marks the second American pulled for care during the outbreak, following an earlier case of an American doctor in Congo. A Kenyan plan to relocate exposed Americans overseas has been blocked by court, while a Bundibugyo-focused clinical trial began earlier this month, offering cautious hope.

article.articleHeadline: कोरोना की खामोश एंट्री: भनक तक नहीं लगी, सामने आए 335 केस, 2 की जान भी चली गई
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Silent Entry of Coronavirus: Not Even a Hint Was Detected, 335 Cases Emerged, Two Lives Lost.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in India: Tamil Nadu reports 335 confirmed cases in 2026, detected during routine hospital surveillance under the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme, with no surge or outbreak indicated. Pune NIV whole-genome sequencing characterizes the circulating variant as very weak, causing only mild symptoms and limited community spread. According to Tamil Nadu, 2024: 990 cases; 2025: 1,250; 2026 so far: 335. In Andhra Pradesh, two deaths linked to COVID-19 are reported: a 52-year-old with diabetes and kidney disease died after being brought to a private hospital in Vellore with COVID-19 and Klebsiella pneumoniae and ARDS; a 46-year-old in Kadapa district reportedly died of COVID-19 with investigation ongoing. A 68-year-old in Vellore died of colon cancer, with COVID-19 infection detected incidentally. Authorities urge calm, rely on official updates, and advise precautions for the elderly, pregnant, and immunocompromised individuals.

triage.headline_ja: コロナの静かな侵入：気づかぬうちに335例発生、2人死亡
triage.triage_reason: タミルナードゥ州での通常サーベイランスによる検出で、変異株は弱毒性・軽症中心。当局はアウトブレイクなし、パニック不要と明言しており、IHR・WPRO基準ともに該当なし。

article.articleHeadline: La peste no es una enfermedad erradicada y sigue matando
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The plague is not an eradicated disease and continues to kill.
article.articleSummary: Plague persists in Madagascar and sporadically in the western United States, including Oregon, as of July 13, 2026. Yersinia pestis causes three forms: bubonic (flea-borne, painful swollen lymph nodes), septicemic (blood infection), and pneumonic (lung infection with person-to-person transmission). Without treatment, fatality approaches 100%. Globally, about 3,000 cases are reported annually; Madagascar experiences roughly 250–500 infections per year, with ongoing activity and a major outbreak in 2017. The Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda are also affected. Europe has been plague-free since 1945, but ancient DNA evidence shows the pathogen’s presence long before. Early diagnosis and rapid antibiotic therapy save lives; diagnosis remains a major challenge. Collaborations between Robert Koch Institute and Madagascar’s laboratories aim to strengthen diagnostic capacity to reduce delays that cost lives.

triage.headline_ja: ペストは撲滅された病気ではなく、今も人命を奪い続けている

triage.notes: 本記事は疫学的解説記事であり、マダガスカル・米国オレゴン州の慢性的な流行状況を説明する内容。DRCとウガンダも「影響を受けている」と一般的に言及されているが、具体的な新規発生データはない。対象国リストにないマダガスカル・米国・ウガンダは除外し、DRCのみ含めた。新規シグナルとしての性質は薄く、続報監視の必要性も低い。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Coronavirus cases detected from Uttar Pradesh to Maharashtra–Andhra Pradesh; will COVID-19 return in 2026?
article.articleSummary: As of July 13, 2026, new coronavirus cases have been reported in multiple Indian states. In Uttar Pradesh’s Varanasi, a 27-year-old man was diagnosed at BHU’s Chest and TB Department and is hospitalized, highlighting that transmission persists. In Andhra Pradesh, eight active cases have been recorded, with two recent deaths: a 46-year-old man in Kadapa’s Masapeta and another case in Rajampeta, Annamayya district; samples have been sent for genome sequencing to identify variants. In Maharashtra, Mumbai reported a fresh case, with singer Jaan Kumar Sanu also testing positive and under treatment. Medical science describes the virus as endemic, with antibodies from vaccines and prior infections reducing severity. Authorities have formed rapid response teams and COVID control rooms; hospitals are told to maintain at least 10-bed isolation wards and ensure adequate testing kits, PPE, and N95 masks. No lockdown or mandatory masking is planned; public should remain vigilant.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo, Uganda Battle Deadly Bundibugyo Ebola Outbreak as Health Response Intensifies - Diaspora Digital Media (DDM News) - Nigeria Breaking News, Africa and World News and Updates
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo and Uganda, beginning May 2026, intensified as cases spread to Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo in DR Congo, with Uganda’s capital Kampala also affected. The outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo virus, was declared on May 15, 2026, and the WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17. Transmission occurs through direct contact with infected blood or body fluids; symptoms include fever, weakness, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, and sometimes bleeding. Frontline health workers face elevated risk amid gaps in PPE and infection control. Surveillance, contact tracing, rapid testing, and isolation have been strengthened. Scientific efforts focus on a Bundibugyro-specific vaccine; Oxford University launched a Phase 1 trial, while existing vaccines target Zaire ebolavirus. International agencies (WHO, Africa CDC, US CDC) monitor and coordinate cross-border responses to prevent further spread. No precise case or death counts are provided.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Malaria cases in Mimika reach 86,747 cases.
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Mimika Regency, Central Papua, Indonesia, reached 86,747 cases as of July 13, 2026, after 693,591 people were tested since January 2026. The reporting covers 81 health facilities (26 Puskesmas, 7 hospitals, private clinics, independent practitioners, and small pharmacies) using the real-time e-SISMAL system maintained by the Ministry of Health. The national malaria elimination pathway targets 2,075,723 tests per year by 2028, with elimination targeted for 2030. In 2025 Mimika conducted about 1.3 million tests; in 2026, over 600,000 tests have been performed with the goal of reaching 2 million tests this year. Testing efforts are funded by Mimika’s regional budget (APBD) through programs Tempo Kas Tuntas and Kaka Sehat, with support from the Ministry of Health. Community participation remains crucial: complete treatment, post-treatment blood checks, and environmental hygiene to advance elimination efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Mehrere Brände in Hessen - und ein Ebola-Patient in Frankfurt
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Several fires in Hesse — and an Ebola patient in Frankfurt.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola patient is being treated in Frankfurt am Main, Germany. The patient is an American physician who contracted Ebola in the Congo and was flown to Frankfurt last night on a specialized aircraft, admitted to a University Clinic on a dedicated isolation ward. The Federal Ministry of Health says there is no danger to the public or other patients. Since mid-May, about 650 people have died and at least 1,830 have been infected in the Congo outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo-type Ebola virus, for which there is no licensed vaccine or specific therapy. Earlier in May, another Ebola-infected American was treated in Berlin's Charité and survived. This hospitalization underscores Germany's ongoing international response to the outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Itajaí registra queda de mais de 90% nos casos de dengue em 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Itajaí records a drop of more than 90% in dengue cases in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Itajaí, Santa Catarina, Brazil recorded a drop of more than 90% in dengue cases in the first half of 2026, reflecting the impact of intensified prevention efforts. The decline follows sustained vector control of Aedes aegypti, robust entomological surveillance, and widespread public awareness campaigns emphasizing elimination of mosquito breeding sites. This substantial reduction lowers the risk of dengue transmission for the city and contributes to the evolving picture for the state of Santa Catarina. Health authorities stress that, despite the positive trend, residents must maintain preventive practices—such as removing standing water and using protective measures—to prevent new transmission foci. The report notes dengue indices in Itajaí and the broader Santa Catarina scenario, underscoring the need for continued vigilance and monitoring as core components of public health strategy.

article.articleHeadline: 2nd American infected with Ebola in DRC evacuated to Germany, WHO chief says
article.articleSummary: July 13, 2026 — A second American infected with Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has been evacuated to Germany for care. The patient, a Samaritan's Purse humanitarian aid worker in Bunia, Ituri province, tested positive for Ebola virus disease caused by the Bundibugyo strain and is receiving clinical care and close monitoring from WHO; the individual was not involved in direct patient care at Ebola Treatment Centers, with contact tracing under way. The first American infected, Dr. Peter Stafford, contracted Ebola while treating patients in the DRC and was evacuated to Charité University Hospital in Berlin; his wife and four children were evacuated as high-risk contacts and have since returned to the United States. The DRC outbreak has surpassed 1,900 cases and 700 deaths, most in Ituri; WHO emphasizes protecting frontline responders.

article.articleHeadline: Diagnóstico precoce é a principal arma contra o avanço silencioso das hepatites virais - CBDL
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Early diagnosis is the main weapon against the silent progression of viral hepatitis - CBDL.
article.articleSummary: Brazil faces a silent hepatitis challenge. About one million people live with hepatitis B or C, most unaware of their infection, underscoring the need for routine screening. In the national context, hepatitis C accounts for more than 70% of liver-infection deaths, followed by hepatitis B at around 21%. The biggest obstacle is asymptomatic early disease; chronic hepatitis B and C can progress for decades before warning signs appear. Hepatitis A is transmitted via contaminated water or food and relates to sanitation, while B and C spread primarily through blood, with hepatitis B also capable of sexual transmission. Early diagnosis is key, with simple, rapid tests able to detect viruses in minutes. Vaccination prevents hepatitis B; there is no vaccine for hepatitis C, though modern antivirals cure over 95% when treated promptly. The July Yellow campaign in Brazil emphasizes awareness and screening.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola
article.articleSummary: UK Medicines regulator cleared a newly developed Ebola vaccine for human clinical trials, developed by University of Oxford scientists. Recruitment of volunteers has begun, with the first doses expected to be given to healthy adults in the UK in the coming weeks. The vaccine targets the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which has recorded 1,792 laboratory-confirmed cases and 625 deaths. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which no approved vaccines exist; Bundibugyo is among six Ebola virus species. Experts say the outbreak remains uncontrolled, driven by insecurity and high population movement in conflict areas, underscoring the urgency for a vaccine.

article.articleHeadline: First vaccine for Bundibugyo Ebola hits human trials in Oxford study
article.articleSummary: New Delhi — As of 2026-07-13, Oxford’s ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine has entered Phase 1 safety trials, becoming the first vaccine against Bundibugyo ebolavirus to reach this stage. The trial will assess safety and immune response in 50 healthy volunteers aged 18–55. The candidate uses the same viral-vector platform as the Oxford/AstraZeneca Covid-19 vaccine. Serum Institute of India has manufactured about 620,000 doses for potential future use and supplied 4,000 investigational doses for this Phase I trial. The Bundibugyo outbreak is ongoing, now the third-largest Ebola outbreak on record, with cases continuing to climb. CEPI has committed $8.6 million to advance vaccine development. If Phase 1 succeeds, CEPI expects late-stage trials to generate data for emergency use authorization or licensure in collaboration with Oxford and SII.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola au Haut-Uélé : les services sécuritaires sollicités pour faire respecter les mesures barrières - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Haut-Uele: security forces called upon to enforce barrier measures - ACP.
article.articleSummary: On July 13, 2026, in Isiro, the capital of Haut-Uélé province in northeast Democratic Republic of Congo, security services were ordered by municipal authorities to enforce barrier measures to halt an Ebola outbreak. Charlotte Nesamowa, a leading member of the provincial security committee, said Ebola is also a security issue and that services would disperse those resisting measures, using non-brutal means and focusing on transport rules— notably banning three people on a single motorcycle— and curbing public gatherings. The city urged residents to adhere to preventive measures and to differentiate Ebola from coronavirus. Health authorities are asked to refer suspected cases to Isiro General Hospital or nearby university clinics for appropriate care. Nesamowa emphasized monitoring resistance to barrier measures.

article.articleHeadline: डीएम ने संचारी रोग नियंत्रण अभियान की समीक्षा की
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The District Magistrate reviewed the communicable disease control campaign.
article.articleSummary: Mirzapur, 13 July 2026: District Magistrate Pawan Kumar Gangwar reviewed the communicable disease control campaign and the Dastak door-to-door initiative at the Collectorate, ordering all departments to achieve 100% targets on key indicators. Focussed on vector-borne diseases—dengue, malaria, chikungunya—and tuberculosis, the DM instructed rapid actions in both rural and urban areas: identify water-logged sites, intensify anti-larvae spraying, fogging, and sanitation; educate households to prevent standing water in coolers, pots, tires, and other containers. Under the Dastak drive, teams will compile lists of fever patients and ensure prompt treatment at nearby health centers. Door-to-door surveys should flag individuals with cough for more than two weeks, night fever, or weight loss; sputum tests for suspected TB should be conducted and patients linked to free DOTS treatment and the Nikshay Poshan Yojana. Attendees included CDO Vishal Kumar and CMO Dr. Kirti Kumar Mishra.

article.articleHeadline: أكسفورد تطلق أول تجربة بشرية للقاح سلالة بونديبوجيو من إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Oxford launches the first human trial of a vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Oxford University has launched the first human trial of an Ebola vaccine targeting Bundibugyo virus, in response to the current outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. The Oxford study will assess the safety of the candidate vaccine named Shadox1 BD-PDV and measure immune responses in 50 healthy adults aged 18–55, with recruitment begun and vaccination expected in coming weeks after regulatory approvals. The vaccine uses the same viral-vector platform as the Oxford/AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. Serum Institute of India has produced about 620,000 doses within two weeks and supplied 4,000 experimental doses for early testing. WHO in May prioritized this vaccine alongside RVSV-ZEBOV in the Ebola response. CEPI has committed $8.6 million to advance development, with further trials planned in Uganda and, if successful, steps toward emergency use authorization or full regulatory approval to ensure rapid, affordable global access.

triage.headline_ja: オックスフォード大学、エボラ・ブンディブジョ株ワクチンの初のヒト臨床試験を開始
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国（DRC）とウガンダで進行中のエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行を背景に、国際的な緊急ワクチン開発・臨床試験が進められており、公衆衛生上の重大性と国際的関心が高い。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はオックスフォード大学のワクチン臨床試験だが、その背景にDRC・ウガンダで進行中のエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行がある。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。インドはワクチン製造（Serum Institute of India）に関する記述のみで発生国ではないため除外。UKも同様に発生国ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Reino Unido da luz verde a una vacuna que busca frenar el Ébola | TN8.ni
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UK gives the green light to an Ebola vaccine that aims to curb Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Experimental Ebola vaccine developed by Oxford University will begin human trials in the United Kingdom after regulatory authorization, as part of the response to the Bundibugyo variant outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The first of four vaccines in development to reach clinical testing, the study enrolls 50 healthy volunteers (ages 18–55) and will monitor participants for a year to assess safety and immune response. The vaccine uses the same platform as the Oxford/AstraZeneca COVID-19 shot—a vector based on a modified cold virus carrying Ebola genetic material—to provoke protection without causing disease. As of 13 July 2026, the Congo outbreak has caused 625 deaths and 1,792 confirmed cases; vaccines for this variant are not yet protective. Over 620,000 doses have been produced, with future Africa trials planned in collaboration with Ugandan institutions. Adverse effects are being carefully evaluated before any mass use.

triage.headline_ja: 英国、エボラ抑制を目指すワクチンに承認を与える
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ変異株）アウトブレイクは625人死亡・1792人確定例に達し深刻な公衆衛生上の脅威であり、既存ワクチンが無効な異常事態でIHR基準複数該当かつ国際的関心が高い。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCで進行中のエボラ・ブンディブギョ変異株アウトブレイク（既存ワクチン非対応）への対応として英国オックスフォード大学が開発した新規ワクチンの臨床試験開始を報じるもの。ウガンダは今後の協力先として言及されるが現時点で発生国ではないため対象国リストにも含まれず除外。英国はワクチン試験実施国であり発生国ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Africa's Ebola Response Faces Fresh Pressure as Deadly Outbreak Expands - Diaspora Digital Media (DDM News) - Nigeria Breaking News, Africa and World News and Updates
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo expands with infections spreading to Tshopo and Haut-Uele, joining Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu as of July 11, 2026, with 1,926 confirmed cases and 702 deaths. Cross-border transmission linked to Uganda raises regional preparedness concerns. WHO describes the outbreak as rapidly evolving, with sustained transmission and rising case counts; by July 1, 102 health workers in DR Congo were infected, 25 of them dead. Africa-wide risk remains high due to cross-border movement and limited treatment capacity. In response, WHO, Africa CDC launched a continental preparedness and response plan in June aimed at $518 million to bolster surveillance, testing, contact tracing and frontline support. Scientists have begun a Bundibugyo-specific vaccine effort; University of Oxford initiated the first human trial (Phase 1) for safety and immune response in 50 healthy adults. Urgent action is needed to stop further spread and protect health systems.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカのエボラ対応、致死的な流行拡大を受けて新たな圧力に直面
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのブンディブジョ型エボラ流行が複数州に拡大し、感染者1,926人・死者702人、医療従事者の感染死亡も多数発生。ウガンダへの越境感染リスクとWHO/Africa CDCによる大規模対応計画（5.18億ドル）が示され、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境感染懸念が記載されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。主発生地はDRC国内の複数州（Tshopo, Haut-Uele, Ituri, North/South Kivu）。

article.articleHeadline: गुजरात : चांदीपुरा वायरस से तीन बच्चों की मौत, चार का इलाज जारी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gujarat: Three children have died from Chandipura virus; four are undergoing treatment.
article.articleSummary: Chandipura virus infections in Gujarat: seven confirmed cases, three deaths, four patients under treatment; all affected are under 10 years old. Among the seven, two are in Gandhinagar and two in Vadnagar. Of 27 suspected samples, 7 tested positive, 12 negative, and 8 results awaited as of July 13, 2026. Fever with flu-like symptoms, potentially progressing to acute encephalitis. The virus is a member of the Rhabdoviridae family, Vesiculovirus genus, transmitted by vectors such as mosquitoes, ticks, and flies. Health officials held a Gandhinagar review to coordinate with the Indian Medical Association and pediatricians for treatment, surveillance, and containment; frontline clinicians were urged to admit suspected cases promptly and provide oxygen and ventilatory support. In 2024, Gujarat reported 61 sites with Chandipura virus cases, with vector control and awareness campaigns; the virus was first identified in Chandipur village, Nagpur district, Maharashtra, in 1965.

triage.headline_ja: グジャラート州：チャンディプラウイルス感染により子供3人死亡、4人が治療中
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準のうち「深刻な公衆衛生影響（小児死亡例）」と「異常性（急性脳炎を伴うクラスター発生）」の2つが該当し、WHO通知相当の基準を満たすためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: チャンディプラウイルスはグジャラート州で毎年局地的に発生する既知の疾患だが、今回は10歳未満の小児7例中3例が死亡しており重症度が高い。バングラデシュは発生地域リストに含まれるが記事本文では言及がなく、対象国として確認できないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Cavite student's death linked to septic shock, infection
article.articleSummary: Cavite, Trece Martires City, Hugo Perez Elementary School-Annex: a Grade 4 student died after a deworming activity; the death is linked to an infection that led to septic shock, per the Department of Education (DepEd). The July 2 deworming event, coordinated with the City Health Office, preceded seven other learners experiencing adverse effects; the deceased was hospitalized on July 3 after vomiting. Initial medical findings tie the death to septic shock from infection. DepEd Assistant Secretary Roger Masapol said the investigation is ongoing to determine if the death can be directly attributed to the deworming activity, with safety protocols being reviewed. The boy’s parents have asked the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) to conduct an autopsy. The father says the eight-year-old, with no known medical condition, took a 400-milligram drug. VACC accompanied the family; the Alliance of Concerned Teachers says teachers should not be blamed.

triage.headline_ja: カビテ州の生徒の死亡、敗血症性ショックおよび感染症に関連
triage.triage_reason: 単発の学童死亡例であり、駆虫薬投与と感染症・敗血症性ショックとの因果関係は調査中で不明。感染症としての広がりや人-人感染の証拠はなく、現時点では孤発事例と考えられるため継続観察とする。
triage.notes: 駆虫薬(400mg)投与後の重篤な副反応の可能性も指摘されており、感染症由来かどうかはNBIの解剖結果等の続報を要する。他7名の学童にも副反応が見られたが詳細不明。
